metadata.case_name: CHOI MEI HO v. CHUNG CHIU YING T/A KIN KEE AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Radiologically revealed a fractured dislocation of the 12 thoracic vertebra over the 1st lumbar vertebra.
source: g. Radiologically revealed a fractured dislocation of the 12 thoracic vertebra over the 1st lumbar vertebra.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified fracture of lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: The spinal cord was found to be crushed by the bony injury at the site of dislocation; complete paraplegia with complete loss of sensation from waist down and paralysis of the lower extremities. She is wheelchair-bound. Her deficits are permanent.
injuries.body_part: spinal cord / lower spinal cord (at T12/L1)
source: Luque instrumentation was carried out to stabilize the reduced spine. The spinal cord was found to be crushed by the bony injury at the site of dislocation.
a. She is a complete paraplegia with complete loss of sensation from waist down and paralysis of the lower extremities. She is wheelchair-bound. Her deficits are permanent.
injuries.icd_description: Complete lesion of lumbar spinal cord

injuries.description: One laceration over right parietal region of head.
source: a. One laceration over right parietal region of head.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: Bruises over right forehead, right thigh, left shoulder and upper back.
injuries.body_part: right forehead; right thigh; left shoulder; upper back
source: b. Bruises over right forehead, right thigh, left shoulder and upper back.

injuries.description: Marked angulation of lower thoracic spine with tenderness.
source: c. Marked angulation of lower thoracic spine with tenderness.

injuries.description: Urinary retention on admission; subsequently described as double incontinence requiring intermittent self catheterization and rectal suppositories for bowel movements.
injuries.body_part: bladder / bowel (neurogenic bladder and bowel dysfunction)
source: b. She suffers from double incontinence. Dr Woo says that she has to empty her bladder every 3 to 4 hours by intermittent self catheterization. She has no anrectal sensation and rectal suppositories are needed every few days for her bowel movements. Faecal soiling may still occur.

manifestations.description: Loss of sensation from lower abdomen (at level of iliac crest) downwards involving both lower limbs.
Loss of muscular movement in both lower limbs.
Double incontinence requiring intermittent self catheterization and rectal suppositories; faecal soiling may still occur.
Intermittent painful paresthesia in the proximal segment of both lower limbs, particularly around the groins and the hips.
Needs assistance in getting upright and transferring from wheelchair to bed and vice versa; needs 24 hour care and attention.

Depression characterized by depressive mood, loss of interest, energy and initiative, loss of self esteem, insomnia, poor appetite and impaired cognitive functioning; moderate to severe and likely permanent.

treatments_received: Massage and acupuncture injections (prior to inability to afford)
treatments_future: Medical check-ups (6 monthly and yearly tests)
Hospitalisation as required for pressure sores
Provision and maintenance of special equipment (wheelchair, hospital bed, bath trolley, hoist, calipers, exercising machine, etc.)

losses.description: Wheelchair-bound with complete loss of movement of lower limbs; very restricted mobility.
Needs assistance in getting upright, transferring and requires 24 hour care and attention.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life

losses.description: Loss of earning capacity assessed at 100%; unable to work.
Life expectancy substantially reduced; evidence suggests mean additional life expectancy of 29 years from the accident.
Depression moderate to severe with associated cognitive impairment.

Depression characterized by depressive mood, loss of interest, energy and initiative, loss of self esteem, insomnia, poor appetite and impaired cognitive functioning; moderate to severe and likely permanent.
